# TitleBar

Header: `winui/ui/hosting/TitleBar.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/hosting/TitleBar.hpp`.

A chrome row with an icon, title and subtitle, optional back and pane-toggle (hamburger) buttons, and three content slots (left header, content, right header).

The bar itself takes no focus. The back and pane-toggle buttons (subtle Buttons) and whatever sits in the slots are each their own [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) stop. Use it either as a row at the top of a page, or as the window's caption in a window with [WindowStyle::extend_content_into_title_bar](../tree/window-style.md). In a window, the bar follows it: it keeps the right header clear of the space [Window::caption_insets()](../tree/window.md#caption_insets) reports for the caption buttons, and dims while [Window::active()](../tree/window.md#active) is false. [hit_region()](#hit_region) then tells the host which parts drag the window. [set_caption_insets()](#set_caption_insets) and [set_active()](#set_active) override what the window says, for a bar drawn somewhere other than its own window's caption. The bar has no minimize, maximize or close buttons, since the window keeps its own. It doesn't set the window's title from [title()](#title), so an app sets both.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool>                can_go_back{false};
ui::Control<ui::NavigationFrame>  frame;
ui::Control<ui::NavigationShell>  nav;

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::TitleBar{
        .title                      = "Contoso Notes",
        .subtitle                   = "Preview",
        .icon                       = ui::IconGlyph{0xE70B},
        .back_button_visible        = can_go_back,
        .pane_toggle_button_visible = true,
        .content_alignment          = ui::Alignment::Stretch,
        .on_back_requested          = [&] { frame->go_back(); },
        .on_pane_toggle_requested   = [&] { nav->set_pane_open(!nav->is_pane_open()); },
        .content                    = ui::TextBox{.placeholder_text = "Search", .max_width = 360.0f},
    },
    // ... the page below the bar ...
}});
// Run the window with ui::WindowOptions{.style = {.extend_content_into_title_bar = true}} to make
// the bar the caption; without it the bar is an ordinary row under the standard title bar.
```

## `ui::TitleBar`

A horizontal chrome row: icon, title, subtitle, an optional back/pane-toggle button, and three arbitrary content slots. Builds a [ui::TitleBarControl](#uititlebarcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
using ui::operator""_fr;
ui::Control<ui::NavigationFrame> frame;

window.set_content(ui::Grid{
    .rows    = {ui::AutoSize, 1_fr},
    .content = {
        ui::Cell{.row     = 0,
                 .content = ui::TitleBar{
                     .title               = "Contoso Mail",
                     .subtitle            = "Preview",
                     .icon                = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Mail),
                     .back_button_visible = true,
                     .on_back_requested   = [&] { frame->go_back(); },
                     .content             = ui::AutoSuggestBox{.placeholder_text = "Search", .width = 300.0f},
                 }},
        ui::Cell{.row = 1, .content = ui::NavigationFrame{.control = frame}},
    },
});
```

```cpp
ui::TitleBar{
    .title, .subtitle, .icon, .back_button_visible, .back_button_enabled,
    .pane_toggle_button_visible, .caption_insets, .active, .content_alignment, .style, .margin,
    .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility, .on_back_requested,
    .on_pane_toggle_requested, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus,
    .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .left_header_content, .content,
    .right_header_content
}
```

## `ui::TitleBarControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A chrome row with an icon, title and subtitle, optional back and pane-toggle (hamburger) buttons, and three content slots (left header, content, right header).

The bar itself takes no focus. The back and pane-toggle buttons (subtle Buttons) and whatever sits in the slots are each their own [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) stop. Use it either as a row at the top of a page, or as the window's caption in a window with [WindowStyle::extend_content_into_title_bar](../tree/window-style.md). In a window, the bar follows it: it keeps the right header clear of the space [Window::caption_insets()](../tree/window.md#caption_insets) reports for the caption buttons, and dims while [Window::active()](../tree/window.md#active) is false. [set_caption_insets()](#set_caption_insets) and [set_active()](#set_active) override what the window says, for a bar drawn somewhere other than its own window's caption. ```cpp
ui::Property<bool>                can_go_back{false};

ui::Control<ui::NavigationShell>  nav;

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {

### TitleBarControl

```cpp
TitleBarControl(std::string title = "", std::string subtitle = "")
```

A bar showing [`title`](#title) and, beside it in the secondary text color, [`subtitle`](#subtitle). Both buttons start hidden, the slots empty.

### title

```cpp
const std::string& title() const
```

The primary caption text. Empty draws none.

### set_title

```cpp
void set_title(std::string title)
```

Replaces the title and updates the layout. Does not change the window's title.

### subtitle

```cpp
const std::string& subtitle() const
```

Dimmed secondary text after the title. Empty draws none.

### set_subtitle

```cpp
void set_subtitle(std::string subtitle)
```

Replaces the subtitle and updates the layout.

### icon

```cpp
const IconSource& icon() const
```

The icon left of the title: a glyph at 16 DIPs in the title text's color, or a path or picture fitted into the same 16x16 box. Empty (the default) shows none.

### set_icon

```cpp
void set_icon(IconSource icon)
```

Shows [`icon`](#icon); an empty source removes it and the title moves left into the freed space. Updates the layout.

### content_alignment

```cpp
Alignment content_alignment() const
```

Where the content sits in the space between the title and the right header. Center, the default, keeps the content at its own width, centered. [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch) hands it the whole space, which a search box with a max width wants.

### set_content_alignment

```cpp
void set_content_alignment(Alignment alignment)
```

Changes the content slot's alignment and updates the layout.

### is_back_button_visible

```cpp
bool is_back_button_visible() const
```

Whether the back button is shown; false by default. A hidden button takes no space, is not a [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) stop and is not hit-tested.

### set_back_button_visible

```cpp
void set_back_button_visible(bool visible)
```

Shows or hides the back button and updates the layout.

### is_back_button_enabled

```cpp
bool is_back_button_enabled() const
```

Whether the back button is enabled; true by default. A disabled back button stays visible but grayed, cannot be clicked, and drags the window when the bar is the caption.

### set_back_button_enabled

```cpp
void set_back_button_enabled(bool enabled)
```

Enables or disables the back button ([ButtonControl::set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled)); a disabled bar keeps it disabled either way.

### on_back_requested

```cpp
void on_back_requested(Callback<void()> handler)
```

Fired on a completed click (or Enter/Space) of the back button. It cannot fire while the button is hidden, since a hidden button is not hit-tested. Replaces any previous handler.

### is_pane_toggle_button_visible

```cpp
bool is_pane_toggle_button_visible() const
```

Whether the pane-toggle button is shown; false by default. Typically paired with a [NavigationShell](navigation-shell.md#uinavigationshell) whose own pane button is hidden.

### set_pane_toggle_button_visible

```cpp
void set_pane_toggle_button_visible(bool visible)
```

Shows or hides the pane-toggle button and updates the layout.

### on_pane_toggle_requested

```cpp
void on_pane_toggle_requested(Callback<void()> handler)
```

Fired when the pane-toggle button is clicked. The bar keeps no pane state of its own; the handler opens or closes the pane. Replaces any previous handler.

### set_left_header_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_left_header_content(std::unique_ptr<T> element)
```

The left header: the slot after the buttons and before the icon. Each slot setter takes ownership of an arbitrary [Element](../tree/element.md), replaces (and destroys) what was there, and hands back a non-owning observer, the same shape as [ExpanderControl::set_content()](../layout/expander.md#set_content).

### left_header_content

```cpp
Element* left_header_content() const
```

The left header, or null when the slot is empty. Owned by the bar.

### set_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_content(std::unique_ptr<T> element)
```

The content: the middle slot, between the title and the right header, placed per [content_alignment()](#content_alignment), typically a search box.

### content

```cpp
Element* content() const
```

The middle slot's element, or null. Owned by the bar.

### set_right_header_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_right_header_content(std::unique_ptr<T> element)
```

The right header: the slot at the far end, kept clear of the caption buttons by [caption_insets()](#caption_insets), typically a [PersonPicture](person-picture.md#uipersonpicture) or a settings button.

### right_header_content

```cpp
Element* right_header_content() const
```

The right header, or null. Owned by the bar.

### caption_insets

```cpp
const CaptionInsets& caption_insets() const
```

The caption space the bar keeps free, in DIPs: the value set with [set_caption_insets()](#set_caption_insets), otherwise what the window the bar is in reports ([Window::caption_insets()](../tree/window.md#caption_insets)), all zero outside a window. All zero is a [TitleBar](#uititlebar) inside the content. Anything else also keeps a 48 DIP strip free at the right for dragging the window.

### set_caption_insets

```cpp
void set_caption_insets(std::optional<CaptionInsets> insets)
```

The caption space to leave alone, in place of the window's. std::nullopt (the default) follows the window again. A change updates the layout.

### active

```cpp
bool active() const
```

Whether the bar draws as an active window's caption: the value set with [set_active()](#set_active), otherwise [Window::active()](../tree/window.md#active) of the window the bar is in, true outside a window.

### set_active

```cpp
void set_active(std::optional<bool> active)
```

false dims the bar (to half opacity) the way a deactivated window's caption is dimmed, whatever the window says; std::nullopt (the default) follows the window again. Redraws only on a change.

### hit_region

```cpp
HitRegion hit_region(Point p) const override
```

Caption over the bar's own background. The visible back button (while enabled), the pane toggle and both headers take the press; in the content, the enabled focusable controls do and everything else drags, subject to [Element::title_bar_drag_region()](../tree/element.md#title_bar_drag_region).

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Lists the back and pane-toggle buttons while they show, then the left header, the content and the right header when present. The icon is decoration, not a child: no tab stop, no popups, no automation node.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

UI Automation's Header control type.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

The title, when no explicit accessible name is set.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### attached

```cpp
void attached() override
```

The element joined a window's tree: [window()](../tree/element.md#window) is now that window. Called for the root a window takes and for everything inside it, and for a subtree added to a tree already in a window. No-op by default.

### detached

```cpp
void detached() override
```

The element left a window's tree (moved out of it). No-op by default.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.
